notes_for_review: ANOM-1 IS THE ITEM I MOST WANT CHECKED. A Gauss-Legendre node-ordering bug made the kernel's kept set non-contiguous for T > 1612, worth up to 0.44 bits in the deep tail and 0.013 bits on the whole-band rms. It was caught BY A CONTROL that aborted attempt 2, not by inspection, and the superseded value 0.369045 is recorded rather than deleted. The validator should confirm the fix and that BATCH-010's script is genuinely unaffected.

ANOM-4 IS A DISCRIMINATION CEILING, NOT A TRIUMPH. The n=50 whole-band rms sits BELOW its plug-in floor at 0.97x. The executor's reading -- that the floor plugs in a noisy lambda for the many lambda~1-3 rows dominating that statistic, so the whole band cannot discriminate models better than about 1x the floor -- is the honest one and must not be reported as the exact model beating perfection.

ANOM-2 NARROWS RT-10. alpha has no locus in (4.10), (4.11), (4.22), (4.23) or (4.24); every alpha on page 23 sits inside (4.19), the GOOD-guess threshold. So alpha=2 changes no number in the wrong-guess chain and RT-10's identification, whatever its merits, is not load-bearing for C3.

THE ARGMIN DRIFT PERSISTS but changes character: the exact family SELECTS its own exponent on the whole band (26.00 for n=43, 24.50 for n=50) where the surrogate rejected exactly those values, and the drift is flatter through count>=1000. The measured local log-log slope of G ranges over [17.9, 24.4], which is the range the surrogate's fitted exponent drifted over -- recorded by the executor as observation only.
